tasks.query: A HEAD response that advertises Zstandard content encoding but carries no body should complete normally instead of failing while the decoder is finalized because no compressed bytes reached end-of-frame.

A request using a client-side TLS certificate should still negotiate successfully when server certificate verification is explicitly disabled, rather than failing with a certificate-required read error.
When a caller supplies an explicit multipart boundary in the content-type header, the encoded multipart body should use that exact boundary instead of generating a different delimiter.

A file-like upload wrapper that exposes iteration dynamically should still be recognized as a rewindable stream so a 307 or 308 redirect can resend the body instead of sending an already-consumed empty upload.

Credential lookup from a netrc file must use the actual URL hostname even when the URL contains user information, so credentials for an unintended host are never attached because of manual authority parsing.

Ordinary dictionaries of string HTTP headers should remain accepted by the public request APIs under inline typing, without forcing callers to widen them to a mutable mapping that also permits byte values.
Deserializing an enum from JSON object form must reject malformed object members whose key is not a JSON string instead of accepting a boolean-like key as the variant name.
JSON object keys containing the strings true or false should deserialize into boolean map keys consistently with the existing coercion of stringified integer keys.

The compile-time check for an invalid feature combination should report a normal compiler error without keeping intentionally unparsable Rust source in the crate, because that source breaks static-analysis tools.

Converting a decimal tree value with an enormous exponent into an integer must enforce the configured scale safety guard before performing the expensive conversion, preventing a tiny input from causing extreme CPU or memory use.

When a standard exception property is explicitly annotated for a serialization view, deserialization should honor that explicit view restriction instead of always exempting the property from view filtering.
Standard exception properties with multi-word names should deserialize correctly under snake-case or kebab-case property naming, rather than being matched only against hard-coded camel-case names.

If schema generation fails inside a nested attempt and the caller catches that error to fall back, temporary field-name and model-type context must always be removed so later fields do not resolve against stale schema state.
Building a model should not mutate the class's user-provided configuration dictionary by inserting derived validation settings that were not present in the original configuration.
Specialized root models should preserve the core schema metadata attached to their wrapped type instead of dropping that metadata while constructing the model schema.

On older Android versions, the runtime should avoid relying on an operating-system wakeup primitive that Python exposes even though the platform does not actually support it, so the event loop can start successfully.

Reusable worker threads must not retain the context variables of the task that originally spawned them on newer free-threaded Python builds; each submitted job should receive only its intended context.

When a child task fails before signaling that startup completed, re-raising that failure from the parent startup call should preserve the original exception cause and context instead of discarding them while unwrapping an internal exception group.
